answer: Presentations anchor to one zenith block: each signs that block's hash with the head of its nebula, the aggregate of its epoch's public actions. Standing requires a 2,000-credit lock held through a ten-epoch unbonding. Checkers, redrawn each epoch by a zephyr drift from other bands so pairs never repeat, recompute it from the record; all three must match, and a match failing an auditor's replay costs the checker its lock. One honest agent locks 2,000 once; 1,000 fakes lock 2,000,000 and must each build an epoch of actions, since a shared state yields one nebula presented twice, voiding both.
